interpretation.diagram_classification: cosmological / natural-philosophical diagram (a concentric, compartmented circle of correspondences between macrocosm, time and the human body; comparable to the medieval 'sphere of the elements' or 'microcosm' schemes, e.g. in computistic and scientific compilations)
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram sets out the correspondence of the four elements, their qualities, the four seasons and the four humours. The central label "mundus annus homo" (world, year, man) names the three levels the scheme is meant to unify: the cosmos, the cycle of the year and the human being. The outer band gives the elements with their paired qualities: "IGNIS" with "calidur"/"calidus" (hot) and "secca"/"secca" (dry), "AER" with "calidus" and "humidus" (hot and moist), "aqua" with "humidus" and "frigidur"/"frigidus" (moist and cold), and "TERRA" with "frigidus" and "secca" (cold and dry). The inner ring gives the seasons and humours that match them: "AESTAS" (summer) with "colera" (choler), "autumnus" with "melancolia", "uer" (spring) with "sanguis", and "hiemps" (winter) with "humor"/"flegmus" (phlegm). The interlaced arcs in red, yellow and blue join each element to the two qualities it shares with its neighbours, so each quality is shared by two adjacent elements. The scheme therefore shows the cyclical, continuous and mutually dependent structure of the world, time and the human body.
interpretation.evidence: Transcribed labels belong to the standard vocabulary of the four elements (ignis, aer, aqua, terra), the qualities (calidus, humidus, frigidus, siccus), the seasons (aestas, autumnus, hiems, ver) and the humours (colera, melancolia, sanguis, flegma). The central label "mundus annus homo" states the macrocosm-year-microcosm correspondence directly. The concentric layout (outer elements and qualities, inner seasons and humours, centre with the three-term formula) is consistent with this reading. Caveats on Step 1: the labels "secca" and "frigidus/frigidur" and "humidus" are repeated and their assignment to elements is inferred from position. Entries 8 and 16 were transcribed with uncertainty ("TRIGIDUS", "autumnus"), and entries 21 and 22 ("humor", "flegmus") read as upside-down text, so the identification of the winter/phlegm compartment is lower in certainty. The Step 1 relations "connected_to" between adjacent outer compartments are weak readings of shared dividing lines, not true connections. The colour-coding of the arcs has no explicit label and is not interpreted.

interpretation.diagram_classification: medical-computistic diagram (humoral theory linked to the calendar)
interpretation.interpretation: The inner ring pairs each season with a humour, in an order of succession around the circle that follows the cycle of the year: summer with choler, autumn with melancholy, winter with phlegm and spring with blood. This presents the human temperament and its changes as governed by the same qualitative cycle as the seasons and the elements, so that health and disease are understood as a balance or imbalance of qualities, as in humoral medicine.
interpretation.evidence: The labels "AESTAS"/"colera", "autumnus"/"melancolia", "uer"/"sanguis" and "humor"/"flegmus" (with "hiemps") are placed in paired compartments separated by short blue lines, which suggests pairing. The reading of the winter pair is uncertain because of the inverted script and the odd word "humor", which may stand for a quality or may be a label for the humour section rather than a distinct item; this lowers certainty. No source is named, since the specific text behind the diagram cannot be identified with confidence.
